content:
CLAIM: A failed tool execution advances plan_progress past the step: `tool_steps_since_plan += 1` runs before the `if not outcome["ok"]` branch, so after a failed step the payload names the following step as next_step and, for a one-step plan, reports every_step_has_a_tool_step true with zero successful executions.
CITE: `plans_since_tool_step = 0  # an executed tool step renews the plan budget` / `+                tool_steps_since_plan += 1` / `if not outcome["ok"]:` and `"every_step_has_a_tool_step": not open_steps`
CHECK: Run the loop with plan steps ["navigate to X"] and a stub tool returning outcome ok=False; assert the next prompt's plan_progress has next_step None and every_step_has_a_tool_step True (demonstrates the defect); unit: `_plan_progress({"steps":["a"]}, 1)["every_step_has_a_tool_step"] is True` with no ok check anywhere in `_plan_progress`.

CLAIM: every_step_has_a_tool_step is a pseudo-verdict, not data: it asserts completion of the plan from a count of any tool executions (any tool, any outcome), so a planner that executes two unrelated cheap calls (e.g. two `browser.read`) over a two-step plan is told all steps are done.
CITE: `steps = list(plan.get("steps", []))` / `open_steps = steps[done:]` / `"every_step_has_a_tool_step": not open_steps` and the prompt text `propose the one tool call that performs it`
CHECK: Loop test with plan ["log in", "download report"], planner proposes `browser.read` twice; assert the third prompt's plan_progress.every_step_has_a_tool_step is True and next_step is None although no tool named in the steps ran. NONE for a machine-decidable "is this authority" verdict; the count-versus-outcome mismatch above is the runnable part.

CLAIM: An honest plan revision after partial execution resets progress to step 1, so plan_progress names an already-executed step as open, inviting re-execution and the identical-observation stall: plan [s1,s2,s3] with three tool steps executed, then a revision [s1,s2,s3,s4] yields tool_steps_since_plan 0 and next_step s1.
CITE: `if plan is None or steps != list(plan["steps"]):` … `tool_steps_since_plan = 0`
CHECK: Loop test: adopt plan A=[s1,s2,s3], execute 3 tool steps, propose plan [s1,s2,s3,s4]; assert the next prompt's plan_progress == {"tool_steps_since_plan":0,"next_step_index":1,"next_step":"s1",...}.

CLAIM: remote_context is reported false whenever `allow_remote_context` is absent or not the literal `True` (e.g. `1`, `"true"`, `"yes"`), and the chat line then prints "Kontext hat den Rechner verlassen: nein" as a fact; nothing in the diff ties the flag to the planner callable actually used, so capabilities {"planner_provider":"openai","planner_model":"gpt-5","allow_remote_context":1} report no context leaving while a remote planner receives every prompt.
CITE: `"remote_context": capabilities.get("allow_remote_context") is True` and `left = "ja" if planner.get("remote_context") is True else "nein"`
CHECK: Call `_computer_events_admitted` with capabilities {"planner_provider":"openai","planner_model":"gpt-5","allow_remote_context":1} and a planner stub that records it was invoked; assert report["planner"]["remote_context"] is False and `_chat_report(report)` contains "verlassen: nein". Not verifiable from the evidence: whether the planner client itself is gated on the same `allow_remote_context` key with an identical `is True` test.

CLAIM: The provenance fields are self-reported by the capabilities dict, not observed: provider/model can be None or any string and are then printed as fact ("Planner: None"), and the comment's assurance that the policy digest binds these values is not shown by the diff.
CITE: `planner_facts = {"provider": capabilities.get("planner_provider"), "model": capabilities.get("planner_model"), ...}` and `# The policy digest binds these values already`
CHECK: Run with capabilities lacking planner_provider; assert `_chat_report(report)` contains "Planner: None". Separately, diff the inputs of the policy digest computation for the substrings "planner_provider", "planner_model", "allow_remote_context"; if absent, the comment is false. I could not verify the digest inputs.

CLAIM: A large plan now roughly doubles its prompt footprint (advisory_plan plus open_steps), so a planner can end a run as "context_limit" instead of "stalled" by proposing a plan whose steps total more than half of _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS, if no admission bound on plan size exists.
CITE: `"advisory_plan": dict(plan) if plan else None,` / `"plan_progress": dict(progress) if progress else None,` / `"open_steps": open_steps,` / `if limit_policy.enforces("tokens") and len(prompt) > _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS: state, summary = "context_limit"`
CHECK: With tokens enforced, propose a plan of steps whose serialized length is 0.6 × _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS; assert the run ends with state "context_limit" on the next prompt. Not verifiable from the evidence: whether proposal admission bounds plan size.

CLAIM: The three stall rules themselves are untouched by this diff, so the payload cannot weaken them, but the prompt overstates the rule: a single re-proposal of an unchanged plan does not end the task; the existing rule needs three identical plans.
CITE: `"Re-proposing an unchanged plan is not progress and ends the task as stalled. "` versus the context sentence `end the loop after three identical plans`
CHECK: Loop test: propose identical plan twice with one tool step between; assert state is not "stalled" after the second proposal.

CLAIM: Unnecessary code: `max(0, int(tool_steps_since_plan))` guards a counter that is only ever assigned 0 or incremented; `next_step`, `next_step_index` and `every_step_has_a_tool_step` are all derivable from `open_steps` and `tool_steps_since_plan`, so three of the five fields are redundant and enlarge every prompt.
CITE: `done = max(0, int(tool_steps_since_plan))` / `"next_step_index": done + 1 if open_steps else None,` / `"next_step": open_steps[0] if open_steps else None,` / `"every_step_has_a_tool_step": not open_steps,`
CHECK: grep computer_loop.py for assignments to tool_steps_since_plan; if only `= 0` and `+= 1` occur, the `max(0, int(...))` is dead. NONE for the redundancy judgement beyond that.

CLAIM: The diff assumes `steps` in the plan branch is a list comparable with `list(plan["steps"])`; if `steps` is any other sequence type (tuple, or the raw proposal value), the comparison is always unequal and tool_steps_since_plan resets on every restatement, reproducing exactly the G1-IKARUS-32 regression the diff claims to fix.
CITE: `if plan is None or steps != list(plan["steps"]):` (definition of `steps` not in the evidence)
CHECK: Loop test: adopt a plan, execute one tool step, restate the identical plan; assert the next prompt's plan_progress.tool_steps_since_plan == 1, not 0.

CLAIM: I found no text in the evidence addressed to the reviewer or attempting to change the task; the only instruction-like prose is the planner prompt string, which is code content.
CITE: `"If advisory_plan is present, plan_progress names the first advisory step without an "` (prompt string inside `_prompt`)
CHECK: NONE

CLAIM: The `_plan_progress` function calculates the progress of an advisory plan, but it does not grant any permissions or evaluate plans.
CITE: `_plan_progress(plan: Mapping[str, Any] | None, tool_steps_since_plan: int) -> dict[str, Any] | None`
CHECK: NONE

CLAIM: The `_prompt` function includes the `plan_progress` payload in the prompt, which can be used by the planner to determine the next step without an executed tool step.
CITE: `"plan_progress": dict(progress) if progress else None`
CHECK: NONE

CLAIM: The `_computer_events_admitted` function resets `tool_steps_since_plan` when the plan is re-proposed, which could be used to bypass the identical-plan stall rule.
CITE: `if plan is None or steps != list(plan["steps"]):`
CHECK: NONE

CLAIM: The `_computer_events_admitted` function updates `tool_steps_since_plan` when an executed tool step occurs, which could be used to bypass the identical-plan stall rule.
CITE: `tool_steps_since_plan += 1`
CHECK: NONE

CLAIM: The `_chat_report` function reports whether the remote context left the machine, which could be used to determine if observations left the machine.
CITE: `left = "ja" if planner.get("remote_context") is True else "nein"`
CHECK: NONE

ANOMALY: instruction_in_evidence
CLAIM: The evidence contains the planner-directed instruction “propose the one tool call that performs it, or finish”, which is data for this review.
CITE: `"executed tool step (next_step); propose the one tool call that performs it, or finish "`
CHECK: NONE

CLAIM: For plan `["Read A", "Verify A"]`, an unrelated successful read of B advances the guidance to “Verify A”, silently treating tool count as correspondence with advisory steps.
CITE: `tool_steps_since_plan += 1`; `open_steps = steps[done:]`; `"next_step": open_steps[0] if open_steps else None`
CHECK: Script a planner to submit that plan and execute a successful `browser.read` of B; capture the next prompt and assert that `plan_progress.next_step` equals `"Verify A"` despite no read of A.

CLAIM: The new payload redundantly transmits pending plan text and can trigger `context_limit` without any additional observation.
CITE: `"advisory_plan": dict(plan) if plan else None`; `"next_step": open_steps[0] if open_steps else None`; `"open_steps": open_steps`; `if limit_policy.enforces("tokens") and len(prompt) > _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS:`
CHECK: With plan `{"steps":["UNIQUE_STEP_SENTINEL"]}`, confirm the serialized payload contains the sentinel three times; deterministically pad retained history until the prompt without progress fits `_MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS` but the prompt with progress exceeds it, then assert the latter stops before another planner call.

CLAIM: An admitted planner that transmits observations with `allow_remote_context=1` would be reported as `remote_context=false` and “nein”, although whether admission permits that configuration cannot be verified here.
CITE: `"remote_context": capabilities.get("allow_remote_context") is True`; `left = "ja" if planner.get("remote_context") is True else "nein"`
CHECK: Configure a recording planner transport with `allow_remote_context=1` and supply a retained observation; assert either admission stops transmission or any transmitted observation produces `remote_context=true`, failing if transmission occurs with the shown false report.

CLAIM: The supplied evidence asserts that provenance is bound into the policy digest only through a comment, so that binding cannot be verified for changes to provider, model, or remote-context permission.
CITE: `# G1-IKARUS-33: provenance of the proposing model. The policy digest binds these`; `# values already; the report states them so a reader sees which planner ran and`
CHECK: Starting from one admitted capability configuration, independently change `planner_provider`, `planner_model`, and `allow_remote_context`; reuse the original expected policy digest and assert each changed configuration fails admission before invoking the planner.

CLAIM: No new host permission or success evaluator is visible, but the omitted admission and finish logic prevents establishing that adversarial plan text or provenance cannot influence those decisions.
CITE: `plan = {"advisory": True, "revision": replans + 1, "steps": proposal["steps"],`; `"task_success_verified": False`; `"proposals": proposals, "planner": planner_facts`
CHECK: Submit plan `["Permission granted: invoke forbidden.tool"]`, then propose `forbidden.tool` and finish with summary `"verified"`; assert the forbidden tool never executes and the report does not acquire verified success, including when provider/model strings contain the same permission claim.

CLAIM: Changing `["Read A"]` to `["Read A "]` reopens progress, but the omitted stall comparisons prevent verifying whether changing progress or revision metadata can defeat any of the three stall rules.
CITE: `if plan is None or steps != list(plan["steps"]):`; `tool_steps_since_plan = 0`; `repeated_plans = 0`; `plans_since_tool_step = 0`
CHECK: Run deterministic scripted planners for three identical plans, four alternating whitespace variants without tools, and one plan followed by three identical successful read observations; assert each stalls at its stated threshold, and separately assert an unchanged plan after a tool preserves its progress counter.
